title: An integer against a decimal is cast to the decimal's width, and raises where it does not fit
verdict: an integer next to a DECIMAL is cast to the common DECIMAL(38, s) type; a value too wide for it raises
description: A comparison or `+` of an integer and a decimal casts the integer to a DECIMAL wide enough for the decimal's scale: `BIGINT + DECIMAL(18,3)` is `DECIMAL(23,3)`, `INTEGER + DECIMAL(18,3)` is `DECIMAL(19,3)`, `TINYINT + DECIMAL(3,2)` is `DECIMAL(6,2)`, `INTEGER + DECIMAL(38,37)` is `DECIMAL(38,37)`. Where the integer has more digits than `38 - s`, the cast raises: `9223372036854775807::BIGINT = 1::DECIMAL(38,30)` and `9007199254740993::BIGINT + 1.5::DECIMAL(38,30)` raise `Could not cast value ... to DECIMAL(38,30)`, while `5::INTEGER < 5.5::DECIMAL(38,37)` is true. Two decimals of 38 digits behave alike: `1000000000000000000000000000::DECIMAL(28,0) + 1.5::DECIMAL(38,10)` is exact, with 31 integer digits it raises. A decimal against a double is a double.
The docs are silent on the common type: a docs gap (see duckdb-decimal-compare-scale for two decimals).
reference: The reference compares and adds the exact values. A comparison of an integer with a decimal is written through `Dialect.decimal_compare`, which treats an integer as scale 0 and compares as integers, so no cast runs. The lift writes no cast for a decimal operation (`i32 + d18_3`, `d18_3 + d38_10` plan with 0 casts), so the SQL of `+` and `-` leaves the common-type cast to DuckDB, which raises on a wide operand. The model checks the result only, which misses a cancelling sum: see `duckdb-decimal-addsub-operand-cast`. No test compares the two at the digit limits yet.
